For you're welcome, I know there's bitte, bitteschön, willkommen, gern geschechen, and nichts zu danken.

"Bitte" is alwas fine. "Bitteschön" means the same but a bit outdated. "Willkommen" is used differently from the english "you're welcome", it's used to welcome someone to a place or event. "Gern geschechen" is similar to "it was my pleasure". "Nichts zu danken." means "you shouldn't have to thank me", it's used when people thank a lot for a minor favor, it doesn't mean thanking was wrong but maybe it was too excessive.
Bitte being a "You're welcome" is just really confusing for me as it also means "Please". Thanks for the help!
It's pretty much how it's used. Tto answer a "danke" and like to "please" if you ask someone to do something for you.
Compare it to "my pleasure" in English, it'll seem less weird.

Bitte. is standard.

Bitte schön/sehr. is usually in response to Danke schön/sehr.

Willkommen is a greeting, z.B. "Willkommen in Deutschland.", the phrase "jemanden willkommen heißen", or just "Willkommen!".

Gern geschehen. is "my pleasure", literally (gladly happened). This can also be shortened to "Gerne!".

Nichts zu danken is "don't mention it". Similar is "keine Ursache", literally "no cause (to thank me)".
